title: SC$^{2}$-WM: A Self-Correcting World Model with Closed-Loop Feedback for Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments
claim: Open-loop methods act without validation and classical feedback uses external error; ours derives internal feedback from foresight to correct latent state before acting.
layout: 3 panels: two top, one wide bottom; left-to-right flow, green highlighted ours
description: Three boxed panels compare control schemes. Top-left (a) shows conventional open-loop VLN: instruction and observation icons feed a policy box, which outputs an action to a robot and a room image, with no feedback. Top-right (b) shows a classical closed-loop control diagram: inputs enter a summation node with an error signal, then a controller, action and output, with a black feedback line returning from the output to the summation node. Bottom (c), outlined in green and the largest panel, shows the proposed method. Latent state s_t passes through a globe-icon world model to produce foresight prediction. A delta node compares this with s_t and sends orange internal feedback to produce a refined state. A green arrow loops back to the world model, labeled adaptation. The refined state goes to the policy, then the action and environment. Green and orange highlight the new parts.
caption: Comparison of (a) conventional open-loop VLN framework, (b) classical closed-loop control, and (c) our self-correcting world model with closed-loop feedback. Unlike open-loop methods that execute actions without validation, SC2-WM leverages internal feedback derived from foresight prediction to refine latent states before action execution.
abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) requires agents to make fine-grained navigation decisions under partial observability. However, most existing methods rely on open-loop execution, lacking mechanisms to detect and correct internal state drift during inference. We propose SC$^{2}$-WM, a self-correcting world model framework that introduces internal feedback for closed-loop decision making in VLN-CE. Our method derives feedback from world-model foresight to perform state-level plan refinement before action execution. To handle challenging scenarios, we further introduce conditional world-aware adaptation, which enables model-level correction by selectively updating the world model at test time when feedback indicates model capacity insufficiency. Experiments on standard VLN-CE benchmarks demonstrate improved navigation robustness and generalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/sunrise-ikun/SC2_WM.
